question.text: In an organ pipe whose one end is at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, the pressure is expressed by <math> <mrow> <mtext>p</mtext> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mtext>p</mtext> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <mo>cos</mo> <mfrac> <mrow> <mn>3</mn> <mi>π</mi> <mtext>x</mtext> </mrow> <mrow> <mn>2</mn> </mrow> </mfrac> <mo>sin</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mn>0</mn> <mn>0</mn> <mi>π</mi> <mtext>t</mtext> </mrow> </math> where x is in meter and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> in seconds. The organ pipe can be

options.text: Closed at one end, open at another with length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>
Open at both ends, length =1 m
Closed at both ends, length =2 m
Closed at end, open at another with length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mtext>m</mtext></math>

solution.text:
For  x = λ

    3 π x 2 = 2 π

⇒    λ = 4 3

at x = 0

there is a pressure antinode. So first end must be close and in case of close at bot end

l⁡ = n λ 2 ⇒ l⁡ = 2 n 3

for close at one end

l⁡ = 2 n + 1 λ 4 = 2 n + 1 3

So for close at one end possible lengths are

2 n + 1 3 = 1 3 ,   1 ,   5 3 ,   7 3

Open at both ends is not possible for close at both end possible length are

2 n 3 = 2 3 ,  4 3 ,  2 ,  8 3 ...... so only possibility is (3)
